content.text: In Nigeria and many other countries, digital creators face a significant infrastructure problem: Stripe, a leading online [[LINK:https://coremerch.github.io/store/blog/payment-options-ethiopian-digital-creators-how-one-creator-2|payment]] processing platform, operates in only 46 countries out of 195 on earth, leaving creators in restricted countries without a reliable way to sell digital products and receive payments. This limitation forces them to seek alternatives, highlighting the need for sovereign commerce infrastructure.

content.text: What This Actually Is and Why It Matters: Stripe alternatives

Sovereign commerce infrastructure refers to the base-layer technology that enables digital creators to sell their products without relying on platforms like Stripe or PayPal. This infrastructure is crucial for creators in restricted countries, as it provides a permanent structural alternative to traditional payment processing platforms. By owning their infrastructure, creators can ensure that their businesses are not dependent on third-party services that may be unavailable or unreliable in their region.
How the Architecture Works Under the Hood

The [[LINK:https://coremerch.github.io/store/blog/real-architecture-behind-selling-music-online-accepting-bitcoin-12|The Real]] of sovereign commerce infrastructure typically involves a combination of free and paid tools, including hosting services like GitHub Pages or Cloudflare Pages, backend logic tools like Cloudflare Workers or [[LINK:https://coremerch.github.io/store/blog/google-apps-script-digital-commerce-automation-what-actually-17|COREMERCH guide to google]] Apps Script, and payment processing platforms like NOWPayments. These tools work together to provide a seamless and secure payment processing experience for creators and their customers. For example, NOWPayments supports over 300 cryptocurrencies and charges a low fee of 0.5%, making it an attractive option for creators who want to accept cryptocurrency payments.
Who This Is Built For and Why

Sovereign commerce infrastructure is built for digital creators in countries where traditional payment processing platforms are unavailable or severely restricted. These creators, who sell digital products like ebooks, courses, and software, need a reliable way to receive payments from their customers. By using sovereign commerce infrastructure, creators can take control of their payment processing and ensure that their businesses are not disrupted by platform restrictions or suspensions. In fact, a PayPal account suspension can hold funds for up to 180 days with no appeal, highlighting the importance of having a reliable and independent payment processing system.
Sovereign commerce infrastructure provides a permanent structural alternative to traditional payment processing platforms.
The Components That Make It Work Together

The components of sovereign commerce infrastructure include hosting, backend logic, payment processing, and storage. For example, the Edge Commerce Stack ($197) includes Cloudflare Pages for hosting, Cloudflare Workers for backend logic, Supabase for storage, and NOWPayments for payment processing. This stack provides a comprehensive solution for creators who want to sell digital products and receive payments without relying on traditional platforms. The Edge Commerce Stack is deployed in 48 hours and includes 5 products loaded, SPF/DKIM/DMARC configured, and end-to-end testing before handoff, ensuring a seamless and secure payment processing experience.

They can then configure their backend logic using Cloudflare Workers or Google Apps Script and set up their storage using Supabase or Google Sheets.
